questions.question: Distinguish between economic growth and economic development. Describe three ways development can damage the environment in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Growth is an increase in the production of goods and services (real GDP). Development is an improvement in the standard of living and well-being of people, including health, education, services, opportunities and fair sharing of benefits. Damage: air pollution from coal-fired power stations, vehicles and household burning (Mpumalanga Highveld); water pollution from untreated sewage, farm chemicals, factory waste and acid mine drainage; land degradation from erosion, urban sprawl, illegal dumping and abandoned mines; loss of biodiversity; climate change from greenhouse gas emissions.

questions.question: Define unemployment and the labour force. The labour force is 24 million and 8 million people are unemployed: calculate the unemployment rate. Distinguish between structural and cyclical unemployment and give two effects of unemployment.
questions.expected_answer: Unemployment: people able and willing to work and actively looking for work who cannot find a job. Labour force: the employed plus the unemployed. Rate = 8 ÷ 24 × 100 ≈ 33,3%. Structural unemployment: skills of workers do not match available jobs, often after the economy changes (mine closures, automation). Cyclical unemployment: job losses during a recession when demand falls. Effects: loss of income and poverty; stress and loss of skills; crime and social unrest; lower tax revenue and higher grant spending; wasted labour and lower output.

questions.question: Define sustainable development and explain, with four examples, how resources can be used productively to promote a healthy environment and create jobs.
questions.expected_answer: Sustainable development meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs (Brundtland Report, 1987), balancing economic growth, social fairness and environmental protection. Examples: fixing water leaks, drip irrigation and rainwater harvesting; energy efficiency and renewable energy (solar, wind), creating installation jobs; the waste hierarchy — reduce, reuse, recycle — with waste pickers and recycling businesses earning income; rehabilitating mined land and protecting wetlands; clearing invasive alien plants (Working for Water) to save water and create jobs.
